name: Vault Street
steps: Open vaultstreet.fun/whitelist and sign in with X. The site says: "We only read your name, username and profile picture."
Like, repost and comment on the pinned post: "Interact with our pinned post on X."
"Post a tweet, thread or art about Vault Street and tag" its account @VaultStreet_rh, then paste the link to your post.

The game opens on 22 October at 17:00 UTC: "Open vaultstreet.fun/play, tap Connect wallet and sign a free message." Then you buy a bank, which the game calls a Treasury: "Pick one of 5 Treasuries ($2 to $45). It's your bank, yours forever, one per wallet."
what: Vault Street Tycoon, a paid bank game on Robinhood Chain, launches 22 Oct. No airdrop is promised; its NFT whitelist is free. Steps, costs and risks.
behind: Nobody we could find. The site's only owner line is "© 2026 Vault Street Tycoon", with no person, company, address or contact email. The X account @VaultStreet_rh, which links to vaultstreet.fun, is the only official channel; there's no Telegram or Discord. No funding has been announced. It has no connection we could find to Resolv Labs' Vault Street. Get the next airdrop first We post new guides,
costs: The whitelist is free. The game isn't: "ETH, once: your Treasury is bought with ETH on Robinhood Chain." That money goes to the team: "Paid in ETH to the team, to fund development and the game's servers." Everything after that costs $VST, and "Prices are listed in dollars and paid in $VST at 1,000 $VST per $1." Getting tokens out costs more. You need 10,000 $VST in your wallet before you can claim
risks: The team is anonymous. The site names no company and has no terms of service or privacy policy, so there's no list of excluded countries, age limit or KYC rule. It's brand new: the X account was created on 10 October 2026, twelve days before launch. No contracts are out yet: "Contract addresses are published here at launch." No audit is mentioned.
